anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.text:
The existing resolver fits better because it is already the one path the report view reads settings through. `settings/resolver.ts:12` owns the defaults for the existing settings, and I traced those resolved values to where `ui/report-view.ts:30` consumes them. A new key there reaches the view through wiring that already works. A view-local settings object would create a second source of defaults beside the resolver. Every later report-view setting would then need a choice between the two paths. So the plan is to add the setting as a resolver key, with its default defined at `settings/resolver.ts:12`.

What should happen to the active report filters when the user switches workspaces?
A) Clear them on every switch, with no setting needed for this.
B) Clear them on switch by default, and add a setting so users can keep today's carry-over.
C) Keep them on switch by default, and add a setting so users can clear them instead.
D) Remember filters per workspace and restore each workspace's own filters on return.
other - name it
Recommendation: B - clearing by default stops the hidden rows you described, and the resolver key keeps today's carry-over available to anyone who relies on it.

That settles ownership, but not what should happen to active filters when the workspace changes. Which behavior should the setting support?
A) Preserve filters by default, with an option to reset them on workspace changes.
B) Reset filters by default, with an option to preserve them.
C) Always reset filters on workspace changes, without adding a setting.
D) Other - name it.
Recommendation: B - it addresses the reported hidden-row problem by default while retaining an opt-in to the current behavior.
